title: Cost control, EMR Serverless, architecture trade-offs
exp: Cost and architecture decisions distinguish a developer who built a Spark job from one who can own a production data platform. These are Lead I questions.
pts: Spot fleet with multiple instance types for better availability.
EMR Serverless: no cluster; pay per vCPU-second; ~30-90s cold start. Best for infrequent jobs.
AWS Glue: serverless ETL, simpler for small jobs, less control than EMR.
When Spark is overkill: a 50MB CSV daily does not need EMR -- pandas on Lambda is simpler and cheaper.

viz.note: Decision matrix: 50MB daily -> pandas Lambda. 10GB daily -> small EMR. 1TB daily -> EMR transient. 10TB hourly -> EMR persistent with auto-scaling task nodes.

qa.q: When would you choose EMR Serverless over EMR on EC2?
qa.a: EMR Serverless for infrequent jobs, variable workloads, teams with no cluster expertise, pay-per-use billing. EMR on EC2 for frequent jobs where a persistent cluster amortizes startup, complex tuning, Spot strategies. The JD's 50-source daily pipeline with hours of processing favors EMR on EC2.

When data fits in memory on one machine. Spark adds startup overhead (2-10 min), operational complexity, higher cost. A 50MB CSV daily is better served by pandas on Lambda. Use Spark when data genuinely does not fit on one machine.
